Okay, I've just finished a series of edits aimed at improving how the CLI handles casual greetings. In `tui.tsx` I added a comment clarifying that obvious small talk is filtered locally, preventing the goal reviewer from kicking in on a simple “hi”. I also tweaked the auto-goal logic to only fire when the prompt isn’t a greeting and the effort level is high or above. In `prompts.ts` I explicitly added a working‑style rule: casual conversation gets a brief, friendly reply and no tools are invoked. The type‑check passed, and I verified the UI renders correctly with a quick tmux smoke test that printed the status line (showing the ultracode effort, etc.).

Now I need to confirm that the new behavior actually works at runtime. Specifically, I want to make sure that when a user types a greeting like “hi”, the system replies with a short message, does **not** set an auto‑goal, and still renders the TPS (ticks‑per‑second) counter in the status bar. The easiest way to do that is to reuse the tmux session I already started (`glinttest`). I can send the string “hi” followed by Enter, give the agent a little time to process (say 12 seconds, which should be enough for the brief reply to appear), and then capture the last few lines of the pane to inspect the output.

I’ll use `tmux send-keys` to inject the greeting, then `sleep` to wait, and finally `tmux capture-pane -p` piped to `tail -25` so I see the relevant portion of the transcript, including any notice messages and the status line. This will let me verify that there’s no “auto‑goal set” notice and that the TPS counter still shows up. That’s exactly the next step.

arguments.command: tmux send-keys -t glinttest 'hi' Enter && sleep 12 && tmux capture-pane -t glinttest -p | tail -25
arguments.description: Send greeting, verify no auto-goal and tps renders
